paragraphs.text: Lhurgoyf is a creature type used for cards that depict a species of large, reptilian creatures, with distinctive elongated limbs and large, toothed mouths. They come in a wide variety of shapes depending on their scavenged sustenance of choice.

Lhuggoyfs appear in all colors , although the "Lhurgoyf" ability ( This creature's power and toughness are equal to the number of cards in your/all graveyards ) nowadays is primary in green , secondary in black . The ability is tertiary in white , blue , and red .
The name "Lhurgoyf" doesn't mean anything. It was made up by the Ice Age team because it "sounded Scandinavian."

The first card to bear the subtype was the classical Lhurgoyf in Ice Age . Lhurgoyf's power is equal to the number of creature cards in all graveyards, and its toughness is equal to that number plus 1. The type returned in Odyssey (see the section on cycles below). The flavor text for the original printing became a classic Magic reference, inspiring various future cards: Ach! Hans, Run! ( Unhinged ), Revenant ( Stronghold ), Saffi Eriksdotter ( Time Spiral ) and Hans Eriksson ( Commander Legends ).
More Lhurgoyfs were printed in Planar Chaos ( Detritivore ) and Future Sight ( Tarmogoyf ).
Lhurgoyfs returned in Modern Horizons 2 , which included Necrogoyf and the first goyf typal/kindred enchantment.
Dominaria United featured Urborg Lhurgoyf , the first goyf in more than one color, and the first to only care about your own graveyard.

MH3 Commander introduced the first cards to create Lhurgoyf tokens: Disa the Restless and Tarmogoyf Nest . It also included three new monocolored lhurgoyfs which all scale using the same ability as Tarmogoyf ( Barrowgoyf , Pyrogoyf , and Polygoyf ). Modern Horizons 3 also had Nethergoyf , a lhurgoyf more aggressively costed than Tarmogoyf and with built-in recursion, but at the cost of considering only its controller's graveyard when setting its power and toughness.
Edge of Eternities featured the elemental Cosmogoyf . The Cosmogoyf is currently the only Lhurgoyf to use exile to define its power and toughness instead of the graveyard .
Odyssey printed a cycle of rare Lhurgoyfs.

Lhurgoyfs spread across Dominaria during the Ice Age , when they adapted to dwindling food resources by developing a carrion-based diet. After the weather warmed, they migrated north and are now found in the plane's arctic Northland . Dominarian lhurgoyfs include the following:
Cantivores which derive power from magical energy.
Magnivores which derive power from emotions.
Tarmogoyfs are omnivorous lhurgoyfs capable of metabolizing a variety of creatures and magics. The scourge of any food chain they encounters, tarmogoyfs' musculatures thrive on a diverse diet.
By the time of the New Phyrexian Invasion , at least one lhurgoyf was to be found in Urborg .
All Lhurgoyfs are star creatures which care about the graveyard to depict their nature as scavengers.

The MH3 Commander deck Graveyard Overdrive featured a minor Lhurgoyf theme. The deck's commander Disa the Restless is also able to put goyfs that are put into the graveyard from anywhere other than the battlefield onto the battlefield. Altar of the Goyf and Pyrogoyf also provide Lhurgoyf synergy.
Modern Horizons 2 included Altar of the Goyf , the first goyf kindred enchantment.
Modern Horizons 3 introduced the first Lhurgoyf kindred Aura in Tarmogoyf Nest .

While Magnivore had seen tournament play, Tarmogoyf's efficiency became a benchmark for creature power in non-rotating formats for more than a decade. Due to the remarkable speed at which Tarmogoyf could grow and its performance in top-tier decks, it became a much sought-after card. Its legacy eclipsed that of the original Llurgoyfs, as most references to "Goyfs" now associate the name and type with multiple card types. Decks featuring Tarmogoyf became known as Goyf-decks.
Tarmogoyf had a reputation for being the strongest creature ever, and playtest card Chimney Goyf paid it homage by merging it with one of the weakest creatures ever ( Chimney Imp ).
